narrative: The model estimates your chance of leaving at 46.0%. In this promotion review, that risk was treated as high enough to deny the promotion: the organisation sees a meaningful possibility you will not stay, so it is reluctant to commit a promotion now. The strongest signal in your case was your total years of experience, and it actually pushed toward staying; your 1–5 years is common among employees predicted to stay, about half of them. The next most influential signal was that you have other job opportunities, and this pushed toward leaving; only about one in four employees predicted to stay reported such opportunities. Your sector, classified as other, was the third signal and added a smaller push toward leaving; roughly one in five stayers work in that sector. Other parts of your profile, such as not feeling you received the deserved promotion, not being satisfied with the job, psychological exhaustion, low job support, no recognition, and no bonus, reinforce a retention concern even though they were not the top three in this explanation. Next, you and your manager should discuss what would make staying worthwhile: a clear promotion path, recognition, support, development, and fair rewards. The organisation should consider a retention conversation before making a final promotion decision.
